import ctypes
import sys

# Define a C function to check endianness
c_code = '''
#include <stdio.h>

int little_endian_p() {
    unsigned int x = 1;
    char *c = (char*)&x;
    return (int)*c;
}
'''

# Write the C code to a temporary file
with open('endianness.c', 'w') as f:
    f.write(c_code)

# Compile the C code into a shared library
import subprocess
subprocess.run(['gcc', '-shared', '-o', 'libendianness.so', '-fPIC', 'endianness.c'], check=True)

# Load the compiled shared library
endianness_lib = ctypes.CDLL('./libendianness.so')

# Define the function prototype
little_endian_p = endianness_lib.little_endian_p
little_endian_p.restype = ctypes.c_int

# Function to check if the system is little-endian
def is_little_endian():
    return bool(little_endian_p())

# Test cases
def assert_test():
    # Check the endianness of the system
    result = is_little_endian()
    # Assert the result is a boolean
    assert isinstance(result, bool), 'Result should be a boolean.'
    # Assert the result is either True or False
    assert result in [True, False], 'Result should be either True or False.'

if __name__ == '__main__':
    assert_test()
